data.title: ACA marketplace premiums rising by 13% in 2027
data.description:
• Health insurance premiums on state marketplaces will increase by an average of 13% for silver tier plans, according to a new analysis.
  • Insurers had proposed an average 15% hike. 
  • In states that run their marketplaces, the silver benchmark premium will rise an average of 16%, while in states where it is federally operated, the increase is 11%, the health policy organization KFF found.
  • Last year, the overall hike was 26%
  • "In their rate filings, insurers point to a higher-than-usual increase in the underlying cost of care, which is not unique to the ACA Marketplaces; some employer plans have also seen steep cost increases," KFF says.
  • The organization added that ACA enrollment declined in 2026 as enhanced income tax credits expired. Those with incomes above 400% of the federal poverty level may face difficulty getting coverage in 2027 as they no longer qualify for premium tax credits and must pay the full cost, KFF noted.

data.title: Centerra outlines Thompson Creek first production by mid-2027 while lowering Mount Milligan 2026 AISC guidance to $1,100-$1,200 per ounce
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Centerra Gold Inc. (CG:CA; CGAU) Q3 2026

Management View

  • “Our third quarter results reflect continued consistent execution at our operations.” (President, CEO & Director Paul Botond Tomory)
  • “Strong copper byproduct credits have enabled us to lower Mount Milligan's full year guidance for all-in sustaining costs.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • “In the third quarter, we completed a record $53 million in share buybacks, bringing our year-to-date total share repurchases to $125 million.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • “Goldfield has achieved an important permitting milestone in the third quarter with all major permits now in place for the Gemfield deposit, which accounts for approximately 80% of the life of mine production.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • “The Goldfield project represents our next source of near-term gold production growth, with first production expected in late 2028.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • “And finally, at Thompson Creek, we remain on track for first molybdenum production in mid-2027, now less than 1 year away and in a very constructive price environment.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • “Adjusted net earnings in the third quarter were $72 million or $0.37 per share.” (Executive VP & CFO Ryan Snyder)
  • “At the end of the quarter, total liquidity was $998 million with $398 million of cash and $600 million available under our corporate credit facility.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)
  • “Turning now to our third quarter operating results, starting with Mount Milligan. Mount Milligan produced over 44,000 ounces of gold in the quarter… Copper production totaled 12.8 million pounds.” (Executive VP & COO Kelly Strong)

Outlook

  • “Year-to-date gold and copper production remains aligned with the PFS mine plan and remain on track to achieve our full year production guidance of 140,000 to 155,000 ounces of gold and 50 million to 60 million pounds of copper.” (Executive VP & COO Strong)
  • “We reaffirm our full year gold production cost guidance of $1,450 to $1,550 per ounce at Mount Milligan, while strong year-to-date copper byproduct credits have enabled us to lower our full year AISC guidance to $1,100 to $1,200 per ounce from $1,200 to $1,300 per ounce.” (Executive VP & COO Strong)
  • “We remain on track to achieve the previously increased full year production guidance of 120,000 to 135,000 ounces of gold.” (Executive VP & COO Strong)
  • “We continue to expect Oksut's full year AISC on a byproduct basis to be within our guidance range of $1,850 to $1,950 per ounce.” (Executive VP & COO Strong)
  • “The project remains in line with the total CapEx estimate of $425 million to $450 million and is on track for first production by mid-2027.” (Executive VP & COO Strong)

Financial Results

  • “In the third quarter, we generated cash flow from operations of $143 million and free cash flow of $17 million.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)
  • “In the quarter, Mount Milligan generated $107 million in cash from operations and $63 million in free cash flow, and Oksut generated $68 million in cash from operations and $66 million in free cash flow.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)
  • “U.S. Moly generated $2.9 million of cash from operations and had a free cash flow deficit of $54 million, mainly related to spending on the Thompson Creek restart project.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)
  • “Consolidated all-in sustaining costs on a byproduct basis in the third quarter were $1,775 per ounce.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)
  • “In the third quarter, sales were over 74,000 ounces of gold and 13.2 million pounds of copper.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)

Q&A

  • Luke Bertozzi, CIBC Capital Markets: “With infrastructure refurbishment approximately 65% complete, what are the main critical path items between now and first production?” Executive Tomory: “We're actually 75% here at the end of October… We'll be in a position to start early commissioning works sometime late in the first quarter… the critical path items are really simple installations and connections and powering up and commissioning.”
  • Luke Bertozzi, CIBC Capital Markets: “Are there any practical opportunities to lock in pricing… to protect early cash flows?” Executive Tomory: “Unfortunately, there's no real forward or hedging market available in molybdenum… it's spot exposure all around.”
  • Luke Bertozzi, CIBC Capital Markets: “How do you think about a minimum cash balance… and how could that influence the pace of buybacks?” Executive Snyder: “We'd like to hold somewhere in the range of $100 million to $200 million of cash… but… we also have the credit facility that we can access if necessary.”
  • Don DeMarco, National Bank Financial: “How should we allocate CapEx over the remaining quarters of development?” Executive Snyder: “I would allocate that pretty evenly between now and the middle of next year… that CapEx range in total is $425 million to $450 million.”
  • Simon Wildsmith, Desjardins: “What's your confidence in landing inside that range… versus the 65% completion?” Executive Snyder: “We still feel pretty good that we're on track for that range… all the key equipment is already on site.”
  • Simon Wildsmith, Desjardins: “Where does the potential review of a U.S. Moly sale or IPO stand?” Executive Tomory: “We continue to do the steps internally to prepare for an IPO or some other separation event, but we're not in a hurry to do that.”
  • Lawson Winder, BofA Securities: “What is a reasonable expectation for U.S. dollar inflation in Turkey?” Executive Snyder: “Going into 2026, we plan for that net inflation to be in the range of 5% to 10%. I think that's roughly where it is… I think that's the prevailing view for next year as well as we go into 2027.”
  • Jeremy Hoy, Canaccord Genuity: “There was a surprise tax cut… Do you expect that to be applicable at Oksut…?” Executive Snyder: “That's our understanding right now… the Turkish government has changed the tax rate from 25% to 12.5% starting at the start of 2027… and therefore, our income tax will step down next year.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly positive, with repeated “solid quarter” framing alongside detailed diligence on execution risk and cash use, including “critical path items,” “cost to complete,” “cost pressure,” and monetization timing for U.S. Moly (CIBC, National Bank, Desjardins, BofA).
  • Management tone was positive and execution-focused in prepared remarks and generally firm in Q&A, using high-certainty language on schedules and capital plans, including “we remain on track,” “we still feel pretty good,” and “we're not in a hurry” (Executives Tomory and Snyder).
  • Versus the prior quarter, Q3 Q&A showed more emphasis on budgeting/inflation framing for 2027 and on U.S. Moly strategic alternatives, while management continued to anchor responses on “self-funded” delivery and timing commitments.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • COO transition became operationally visible in Q3, with “Kelly Strong for his first quarterly operating update as our new Chief Operating Officer.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory) In Q2, management had said, “I'd like to welcome Kelly Strong, who will be joining Centerra as our new Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer in mid-August.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • Share repurchases stepped up in Q3: “we completed a record $53 million in share buybacks” (President, CEO & Director Tomory) versus Q2: “we completed $50 million in share buybacks and approved up to $200 million in share repurchases for the full year 2026.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • Thompson Creek build progress advanced from Q2: “approximately 52% of the infrastructure refurbishment complete” (Q2 speaker listed as Unknown Executive, Interim COO) to Q3: “approximately 65% of the infrastructure refurbishment complete… increasing to 75% complete as of late October.” (Executive VP & COO Strong)
  • Mount Milligan cost guidance language tightened in Q3 with the explicit AISC reduction: “lower our full year AISC guidance to $1,100 to $1,200 per ounce from $1,200 to $1,300 per ounce.” (Executive VP & COO Strong)

Risks and Concerns

  • “Unfortunately, there's no real forward or hedging market available in molybdenum… it's spot exposure all around.” (President, CEO & Director Tomory)
  • “There's obviously high inflation in Turkey… and you end up in a net inflation position on your U.S. dollar cost base… we plan for that net inflation to be in the range of 5% to 10%.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)
  • “Absolute costs are up a little bit… We're probably tracking about 5% higher on absolute costs.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)
  • “Q3 was a bit outsized… because… we had built up inventories at a lower price.” (Executive VP & CFO Snyder)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized consistent operational execution, an increased pace of share repurchases, and multiple development catalysts, while reiterating timelines for Thompson Creek first production in mid-2027 and Goldfield first production in late 2028. The quarter’s investable deltas were the lowered Mount Milligan full-year AISC guidance range, higher visibility on Thompson Creek completion and commissioning steps, and management’s positioning of U.S. Moly as a spot-price-exposed cash flow lever that the company is preparing to potentially separate, without committing to timing.

data.title: GFL investor relations exit unrelated to potential deal - CTFN
data.description:
The exit of a GFL Environmental (GFL) investor relations executive is unrelated to the potential sale of the trash hauler. 

Mario Cortellacci, vice president of investor relations at GFL, is stepping down, according to an internal memo CTFN reported earlier on Friday.

GFL shares were moving higher on Friday as some investors were speculating that his exit could be related to the sales process. The shares closed up 0.4% on Friday.

Cortellacci is leaving the company to take a role as chief of IR at a company going public, according to the report.

The executive departure comes after GFL on Wednesday said in its Q3 earnings release that the board's special committee has given interested parties a final deadline of Nov. 9 to disclose their updated proposals.

 CTFN reported Thursday that a sovereign fund is now involved in the bidding for the waste management company. The new bidder entered the sale process a few weeks ago and is not affiliated with the two consortia bidding for GFL.

data.title: New Break Resources plans C$550K financing to fund Moray gold drilling
data.description:
• New Break Resources (NBRK.CN) announced on Friday that it plans to raise up to C$550K through a non-brokered private placement of 2.5M flow-through shares priced at C$0.22 each.
  • The flow-through proceeds will be used for eligible Canadian exploration expenses, which the company plans to renounce to investors by Dec. 31, 2026.
  • Moreover, the gross proceeds will fund ongoing drilling at the company's Moray gold project in Ontario.
  • Finders may receive a 6% cash fee and warrants equal to 6% of the flow-through shares they place. The warrants will be exercisable at C$0.22 for 24 months.
  • The offering is expected to close within two business days, subject to regulatory approvals.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Seegnal terminates older non-brokered private placements, launches new offering
data.description:
• Seegnal (SEGN:CA) said on Friday that it will terminate its previously announced non-brokered private placement offerings after raising aggregate gross proceeds of C$416,220.
  • The offerings terminated were announced on June 2, 2026; July 21, 2026; August 26, 2026; and October 1, 2026.
  • Following a review of its financing requirements and strategic alternatives, the company determined not to proceed with any additional tranches of the offering, as it is evaluating alternative financing opportunities that it believes may be more suitable for its current objectives, Seegnal said.
  • The company also launched a new non-brokered private placement of up to 1M units for gross proceeds of up to C$1.5M, at a price of $0.15 per unit.
  • Each unit is comprised of one common share and one common share purchase warrant. 
  • Each warrant is exercisable to acquire one common share at a price of C$0.25 for a period of 36 months from the applicable closing date.
  • The company added that it will use the proceeds from the new offering for general corporate and working capital purposes. 
  • All securities issued under the new offering will be subject to a hold period expiring four months and one day from the date of issuance. 
  • The offering is expected to close in one or more tranches on or before December 31, 2026.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Mastech details knowledge-first enterprise strategy as data and AI bookings reach $10.8M
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Mastech Digital, Inc. (MHH) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO Nirav Patel framed a strategic repositioning around AI delivery, saying, "This quarter we announced our vision of the Knowledge-first Enterprise and introduced a new positioning for the Mastech brand." (CEO, President & Director Nirav Patel) He said Mastech’s differentiation is "the ability to turn a client's own data and knowledge into practical, applicable, and scalable AI solutions that deliver outcomes" and added, "we are aligning our offerings, capabilities, and assets around three core offerings: applied AI, modern data, and AI Governance, trust, and safety." (CEO Patel)
  • Patel tied the strategy to partner priorities and scaling beyond pilots, stating, "In this offering, we combine agentic technology with our own engineering talent to move those solutions into production so they scale and are adopted rather than remaining pilots." (CEO Patel) He also said, "We have built this offering anchored by our partnerships in the likes of Snowflake, Azure, and Databricks." (CEO Patel)
  • CFO Kannan Sugantharaman connected the quarter’s data and AI momentum to the company’s EDGE program, saying, "data and AI grew sequentially again this quarter. That's two quarters in a row. And the first time we have done that since 2024." (CFO & COO Kannan Sugantharaman) He added, "We believe this growth shows that EDGE is working." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)

Outlook

  • Management reiterated it will not issue guidance, with Jennifer Lacey stating, "As a reminder, we will not be providing guidance during this call, nor will we provide guidance in any subsequent one-on-one meetings or calls." (Executive VP, Head of Legal, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary Jennifer Lacey)
  • In place of formal guidance, management flagged seasonality and ongoing investment posture. Sugantharaman said, "as we enter the fourth quarter, we expect the seasonal effects that typically affect our industry, including holiday related slowdowns and year-end contract completion." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman) Separately, he said, "We plan to continue to invest significantly in talent, in building competencies, and then expanding our data and AI business." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Versus the prior quarter’s narrative focused on becoming "an AI-first company" and building the "growth office," the current quarter’s outlook language emphasized the new brand/operating model framing; Patel said, "we hope to amplify the brand further over the coming year." (CEO Patel)

Financial Results

  • Sugantharaman reported, "During the third quarter, we delivered consolidated revenue of $42 million, a 13.4% decrease year-over-year compared to the prior year period." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman) He also said, "Gross profit of $12.2 million was a decrease of 10.5% compared to the prior year period, but in gross margin terms, we have seen an improvement of 50 basis points from 40% to 40.5%." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Segment results showed a mixed year-over-year picture with sequential improvement in data and AI. Sugantharaman said, "Our Talent segment delivered revenue of $27.9 million" and "Our data and AI segment reported revenue of $14.1 million" while adding the data and AI segment was "a growth of 4.7% sequentially." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Profitability was described on both GAAP and non-GAAP bases. Sugantharaman said, "GAAP net income for three months ended September 30 was $0.00 per diluted share" and "Non-GAAP net income for the three months ended September 30 was $1.2 million, or $0.10 per diluted share." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Balance sheet and capital allocation comments were centered on liquidity and buybacks. Sugantharaman said, "we had $37.9 million in cash on hand, no bank debt outstanding" and "the entire $5 million remains available under the share repurchase program." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)

Q&A

  • Marc Riddick, Sidoti & Company, LLC: "Maybe you could talk a little bit about how we should view" the Knowledge-first Enterprise and its go-to-market impact? CEO Nirav Patel answered, "we will lead with outcomes, not technology for its own sake" and positioned enterprise knowledge as defensible advantage: "That knowledge is, to us, is the real moat, and it belongs to the enterprise." (CEO Patel)
  • Marc Riddick, Sidoti & Company, LLC: asked about drivers behind sequential data and AI growth and whether any verticals stood out. CEO Patel said client conversations "begin with applied AI conversations, but they quickly turn into getting their data ready for AI" and characterized spend as "disproportionately" oriented to "data modernization and foundation." (CEO Patel) CFO Kannan Sugantharaman added detail on the highlighted win: "It's our largest AI deal to date" and described "an agentic AI audit platform on AWS" with "human in the loop controls." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Marc Riddick, Sidoti & Company, LLC: questioned headcount/investment pacing and whether data and AI headcount could rise. Sugantharaman said, "we are making these investments with a multi-year view" and pointed to flexibility: "we do have $38 million roughly of cash and no debt." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman) He also linked talent changes to client insourcing and exits from lower-margin staffing, stating, "We believe the impact of those factors are largely behind us." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Lisa Thompson, Zacks Investment Research, Inc.: asked whether the three offerings are new capabilities or repackaging. Patel said, "it's a combination of those two" and characterized applied AI as new: "That is a completely new offering." (CEO Patel)
  • Lisa Thompson, Zacks Investment Research, Inc.: asked whether offerings could drive recurring revenue. Patel said, "all things AI are pretty sticky in nature" and added, "we do believe there is a recurring nature of our business." (CEO Patel)
  • Lisa Thompson, Zacks Investment Research, Inc.: asked about optimizing LLM usage and cost. Patel framed client scrutiny as cost-driven, saying, "they're asking the question, show me AI at what cost?" and added that this is driving "efficient AI deployment conversations." (CEO Patel)
  • Lisa Thompson, Zacks Investment Research, Inc.: asked whether the invoice-audit platform can be replicated across industries. Sugantharaman said, "we don't see this as one-off" and added, "Each engagement makes the next one faster and deliver more value to our clients." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was neutral-to-slightly positive, with questions oriented toward commercialization and scalability (go-to-market, vertical mix, recurring revenue, LLM cost tradeoffs), including Thompson’s prompt, "Is there a possibility of having recurring revenues from some of these abilities?" (Lisa Thompson, Zacks Investment Research, Inc.: Question)
  • Management tone was slightly positive and expansion-oriented in prepared remarks, repeatedly using conviction language such as, "We believe this growth shows that EDGE is working" and "We plan to continue to invest significantly." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Compared with the prior quarter, management shifted from emphasizing the "growth office" buildout and partner program launch to a broader narrative around brand positioning; Patel’s current-quarter framing, "we announced our vision of the Knowledge-first Enterprise," replaced the prior quarter’s emphasis on "progress we are making as an AI-first company." (CEO Patel)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The strategic storyline changed from Q2’s focus on specific commercial infrastructure (partner program and growth office functions) to Q3’s explicit repositioning; Patel said Q3 "announced our vision of the Knowledge-first Enterprise," while Q2 highlighted, "we are seeing Frontier Labs" driving spending rotation and described launching "our growth office function." (CEO Patel)
  • Data and AI sequential growth continued in both quarters, but Q3 emphasized repeatability and scaling into production via "applied AI" and "AI governance, trust, and safety," whereas Q2 emphasized an "agentic foundation" engagement and partner-sourced momentum. (CEO Patel)
  • Analyst questioning remained consistent across quarters around commercialization and drivers of demand, but Q3 questions leaned more into packaging/recurring revenue and AI cost efficiency; Patel addressed this directly with, "show me AI at what cost?" (CEO Patel)

Risks and Concerns

  • Demand/seasonality risk into Q4 was explicitly noted: "we expect the seasonal effects that typically affect our industry, including holiday related slowdowns and year-end contract completion." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Talent segment baseline risk from client actions and portfolio pruning continued to be discussed, with Sugantharaman noting insourcing and exits "do lower the baseline going into future quarters," even as he said, "We believe the impact of these factors is now largely behind us." (CFO & COO Sugantharaman)
  • Execution risk around scaling AI beyond pilots was repeatedly referenced as a focus area, with Patel describing the goal of solutions that "scale and are adopted rather than remaining pilots." (CEO Patel)

Final Takeaway

Management positioned Q3 as a strategic rebrand and operating-model pivot toward a “Knowledge-first Enterprise,” emphasizing applied AI, modern data, and AI governance as the core go-to-market structure. Leadership highlighted a second straight quarter of sequential data and AI revenue growth and pointed to a largest-to-date AI deal (agentic audit platform on AWS) as evidence of moving AI work into production. At the same time, management reiterated it will not provide formal guidance, flagged typical Q4 seasonal slowdowns, and continued to describe the talent segment as reset by client insourcing and deliberate exits from lower-margin roles, with liquidity and investment capacity supported by cash and no debt.

data.title: Carter’s forecasts Q4 net sales $860M-$880M as it rolls out new brand relaunch and leadership structure
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Carter’s, Inc. (CRI) Q3 2026

Management View

  • “Carter’s third quarter results exceeded our outlook even as we navigated continued uncertainty and choppiness in the macroeconomic environment,” and management said it reversed early-quarter softness by “refocus[ing] to drive efforts through strategic investments using marketing insights, crisp promotions and targeted merchandising.” (President, CEO & Director Sharon John)
  • “This effort included the multi-touch point introduction of Carter’s new comprehensive branding initiative, marking the first reimagination of the look, feel and promise of the brand in a quarter century,” with a new promise to “let every child’s light shine,” which management positioned as moving Carter’s toward being “a trusted partner for parents” rather than “just being seen as an apparel brand.” (President, CEO & Director John)
  • “In less than two months, our campaign has generated over 1.6 billion media impressions,” and management cited “nearly 20% growth in branded search versus the time period before the launch.” (President, CEO & Director John)
  • “Some financial highlights from the third quarter include net sales of $752 million,” “adjusted operating income of $57 million,” and “adjusted operating margin expansion of 240 basis points,” while management also noted results were “inclusive of the negative revenue impact from the net closure of more than 30 locations in our North American fleet.” (President, CEO & Director John)
  • “For the quarter, we achieved our net sales forecast and exceeded our expectations on profitability,” and management reported “reported earnings per share were $1 compared to $0.32 last year,” while adding it recorded “approximately $1 million in charges related to intellectual property litigation.” (CFO & COO Richard Westenberger)
  • “Comparable retail sales increased 0.4%,” and management said “our most important baby segment deliver[ed] its eighth consecutive quarter of comp sales growth,” while “our older kids business was slightly down versus last year.” (Chief Retail & Digital Officer Allison Peterson)
  • “Third quarter net sales for our Wholesale segment decreased 4%,” which management said was “better than expected,” and management highlighted international momentum with “international net sales increased 4%,” while “International operating income increased 28% over last year to $12 million.” (Chief Retail & Digital Officer Peterson; CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • “We are pleased to have shared earlier today an evolved organizational structure,” including: “Chief Product Officer will be filled by Maria Gemzell,” “Chief Marketing Officer role will be broadened… and retitled as Chief Brand Officer, led by Sarah Crockett,” and “we will be establishing a stand-alone role and conducting a search for a Chief Operating Officer” ahead of “the expected late first quarter 2027 retirement of Karen Smith.” (President, CEO & Director John)

Outlook

  • “We have decided to take a prudent approach with a slight downward adjustment to our fourth quarter revenue outlook,” which management linked to “some of the softness we have seen in our fourth quarter-to-date sales” and “amplified consumer concerns in election years.” (President, CEO & Director John)
  • “For the fourth quarter, we’re forecasting net sales in the range of $860 million to $880 million,” “adjusted operating income… $74 million to $83 million,” and “adjusted fourth quarter EPS… $1.37 to $1.55.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • “We’re now expecting full year net sales in the range of $2.910 billion to $2.93 billion,” and management added, “we’re maintaining our previous outlook for full year adjusted operating income growth in the low single-digit to mid-single-digit range,” while also “maintaining our outlook for adjusted EPS to decline in the high single digits to low double digits.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • “We’ve updated our outlook… to reflect an expectation for more moderate demand than in our previous forecast,” including “moderated our forecast for replenishment demand” in wholesale and adjusted retail assumptions “to reflect current trends.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)

Financial Results

  • “Adjusted gross margin expanded 200 basis points… to 47.1%,” which management attributed to “a higher year-over-year mix of U.S. retail sales and higher realized pricing,” while noting this “offset higher tariff costs and investments in product make,” and adding, “AURs increased mid-single digits, while units decreased mid-single digits.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • “Adjusted SG&A decreased nearly 2%… to $303 million,” and management said “benefits from our productivity initiatives, including store closures, more than offsetting incremental investments in marketing.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • “Third quarter adjusted earnings per share were $1.03,” and management highlighted cash and inventory positioning with “cash on hand and short-term investments of over $525 million” and “net inventories… $587 million, 11% lower than prior year.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • “Year-to-date, we’ve generated operating cash flow of more than $100 million,” and management said free cash flow was “$72 million” versus “negative free cash flow of nearly $180 million” last year, while also noting “we paid $27 million in dividends through the first nine months of the year.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)

Q&A

  • Jay Sole, UBS: Asked about prioritizing wholesale vs. retail and improving store traffic; President, CEO & Director John: “we see… an opportunity to drive synergy… inclusive of both wholesale, retail and e-com,” and described plans for “higher engagement experiences to drive traffic” including “integrated solutions, like… the Stellar Sleep program” and app-based features.
  • Jay Sole, UBS: Asked about new revenue streams beyond apparel; President, CEO & Director John: “we’re looking at the purposeful expansion of the addressable market across 3 different vectors,” including “aging up the consumer,” “pushing up the socioeconomic strata… with our sub-brand Little Planet,” and “an asset-light approach” to global expansion.
  • Kelly Crago, BMO: Pressed on wholesale guide-down and order books/pricing; CFO & COO Westenberger: “the majority… relates more to the U.S. retail business,” and said “we had good demand for the order book for spring 2027,” adding “Spring preships are up about 30% in the fourth quarter.”
  • Irwin Boruchow, Wells Fargo: Asked about Q4 AUR/gross margin trajectory and tariff impacts; CFO & COO Westenberger: “pricing planned up… low single digit in the U.S. retail business in fourth quarter,” and on Q3 gross margin expansion said “About half… had to do with… higher mix… U.S. retail,” while “tariffs were not as meaningful… in the third quarter,” adding for Q4 “it’s $10 million or $11 million of lower gross tariff burden.”
  • James Chartier, Monness Crespi Hardt: Asked about marketing spend and leaning in; CFO & COO Westenberger: “we’re spending about $20 million more on demand creation this year,” and added, “I don’t think we’re at the point of inefficiency yet.”
  • Jonathan Keypour, Goldman Sachs: Requested quarter-to-date comps and margin drivers; CFO & COO Westenberger: “It’s down, John,” and “we’re actually going to move away from providing the intra-quarter data point,” later adding “Cotton is clearly up… about 20%” and warning, “I don’t think we’re out of the woods as it relates to tariffs.”
  • Tom Nikic, Needham: Asked timing for leadership changes to impact results; President, CEO & Director John: “It will come in phases,” adding the new Chief Product Officer “could have quite a strong impact,” and noting “some things can go fast and some things might take a minute.”
  • Tom Nikic, Needham: Asked about holiday promotional risk; Chief Retail & Digital Officer Peterson: “we are absolutely anticipating the promotional environment will intensify with heavy discounting in November and December,” and said the company “considered… a more aggressive promotional environment in our forecast.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • “Slightly negative” analyst tone, concentrated on visibility and pressure points, including: “If you could give us the quarter-to-date comp, please?” and follow-ups probing tariff and input-cost sensitivity such as “Cotton… and how the tariff lapse should influence margins next year?” (Jonathan Keypour, Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.)
  • “Slightly positive” management tone in prepared remarks, emphasizing early brand-relaunch traction: “our campaign has generated over 1.6 billion media impressions,” while also flagging caution: “we… remain cognizant of the continued uncertainty in the macro market environment.” (President, CEO & Director Sharon John)
  • “More cautious” tone in Q&A relative to prepared remarks, highlighted by disclosure tightening and uncertainty language: “we’re… going to move away from providing the intra-quarter data point,” and “too early to probably be more specific on 2027.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s more upbeat framing (“we exceeded our second quarter outlook,” “Net sales grew… up 5%,” and “adjusted operating profit increased 54%”), the current call leaned more on prudence: “we’ve updated our outlook… prudently” and cited “softness… in our fourth quarter-to-date sales.” (President, CEO & Director John; CFO & COO Westenberger)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • In Q2, management highlighted momentum and growth (“Net sales grew… up 5%,” and “comparable sales growth of 5%”), while in Q3 management emphasized stabilization and a late-quarter turnaround (“softness in July and August,” then “September comps were up double digits”). (President, CEO & Director John; Chief Retail & Digital Officer Peterson)
  • Q2 guidance language pointed to tariff-driven margin relief potential (“we may have some upside to our earnings outlook”), while Q3 guidance stressed moderation and prudence (“expectation for more moderate demand,” and Q4 ranges for sales, operating income, and EPS). (CFO & COO Richard Westenberger)
  • Q2 discussion focused on channel and platform enhancements (eCommerce features, marketing activations like “our collaboration with Umbro”), while Q3 centered on brand repositioning (“first reimagination… in a quarter century”) and leadership restructuring (new/expanded C-suite roles and a forthcoming COO search). (Chief Retail & Digital Officer Allison Peterson; President, CEO & Director Sharon John)

Risks and Concerns

  • “Risks we’re monitoring include consumer sentiment and spending given the ongoing pressures of persistent inflation, including the price of gas,” and management added election-related caution: “the upcoming midterms are on our radar.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • Supply chain risk was tied to logistics constraints: “delayed delivery of product from port congestion and container availability issues,” though management said, “To date, these disruptions have not had a meaningful impact on the business.” (CFO & COO Westenberger)
  • Promotional and tariff uncertainty remained active watch items: “we are absolutely anticipating the promotional environment will intensify,” and “I don’t think we’re out of the woods as it relates to potential further changes” in tariffs. (Chief Retail & Digital Officer Peterson; CFO & COO Westenberger)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as an execution-driven recovery from a soft start, fueled by a major Carter’s brand relaunch, targeted September actions, and ongoing productivity work that expanded profitability and supported cash generation. At the same time, leadership described a cautious setup into Q4—lower near-term demand visibility, expected holiday promotional intensity, and persistent tariff/input-cost uncertainty—while positioning a reorganized leadership structure and “three vectors” of addressable-market expansion (age-up, socioeconomic expansion via Little Planet, and asset-light international growth) as the foundation for its post–year-end strategic update.

data.title: Inovio surges 280% following FDA approval of Voceryq for rare disease
data.description:
• Inovio Pharmaceuticals (INO) is up ~280% in after-hours trading Friday after the US FDA announced it has approved Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) as a treatment for the rare disease recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP).
  • The approval is the first for a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the US.
  • RRP is characterized by small, wart-like growths in the airways. The condition is caused by human papillomavirus.
  • Accelerated approval was granted based on data indicating that Voceryq helped reduce the frequency of surgical procedures needed to remove growths in adults, meeting an intermediate clinical endpoint.
  • Inovio will need to conduct a post-marketing study to confirm the therapy's benefit.
  • The FDA said that the treatment is "designed to stimulate the immune system to respond to and attack cells infected by the specific types of HPV that cause RRP (types 6 and 11)."

data.title: Textron’s unit wins $114.7M Navy contract boost for Marine helicopters
data.description:
• Bell Textron, a subsidiary of Textron (TXT), received a $114.7M U.S. Navy contract modification to upgrade the electrical systems and structures of Marine Corps AH-1Z and UH-1Y helicopters.
  • The award covers 15 A-kits, four mission kits, nine aircraft installations, components, materials, and spare parts.
  • The work is expected to be completed by June 2028.
  • The full $114.7M will be funded through FY2027 Navy aircraft procurement funds.
  • Naval Air Systems Command is the contracting activity.

data.title: Accendra Health gets NYSE non-compliance notice
data.description:
• Accendra Health (ACH) said on Friday that on October 27, 2026, it received a notice from the New York Stock Exchange about non-compliance with the exchange's continued listing standards.
  • The company said it intends to respond to the NYSE within 10 business days of receipt of the notice affirming its intent to submit a business plan.
